Moreover, a few HVSs are outliers in the overall standard Hills picture, as HE0437-5439, a  9 M_{\odot}  B-type main-sequence whose travel time is longer than its main sequence lifetime (Edelmann et al. 2005).

Most of the observed HVSSs support the standard Hills scenario, but the  \sim9M_{\odot}  main-sequence HVS HE0437-543 and the candidate HVB require different production mechanisms than the standard binary disruption.

notes: HE0437-5439: At T:p7-b8 the identifier is printed as HE0437-543 (missing the final 9); the matching description identifies it as the same star, not an additional object. The paper's final assessment favors an LMC origin but continues to describe it as an observed HVS. The unnamed candidate HVB from Németh et al. (2016) mentioned at T:p1-b5 and T:p1-b10 is a binary system with no individual stellar identifier in the supplied text, so no separate entry is made.

HE0437-5439: The paper discusses HE0437-5439 only as a literature example, not as one of its simulated quadruple systems. The reported values are approximate. No right ascension, declination, parallax, proper motion, galactocentric radius, Galactic-rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability is reported for this star. Relevant passage: T:p1-b5.
